How it works

Your eyes, then AGENCY, then done.

  1. 1

    You look

    Your Mac's camera follows your eyes. Hold your look on a big choice and it fills up, then selects. A quick glance across does nothing. The video never leaves your Mac.

  2. 2

    AGENCY works

    It asks only what it doesn't know, plans the steps, and does them in your real apps. Before anything that matters, it stops and shows you exactly what will happen.

  3. 3

    It's done, and checked

    AGENCY confirms the result really happened, says so plainly, and tells you if something went wrong and what it will try next.

Next: Features

Features

Everything a day needs, a few looks away.

Each feature says where it really stands, as of 10 October 2026. “Works in the prototype today” means it runs and is tested in the AGENCY prototype in our repository. “Being built” means it's in progress for AGENCY OS.

◔Being built

A calm Home that knows your usuals

Home is a screen of big choices: Talk, Call someone, Food, Papers, Shopping, Messages, Watch & listen, Browse, Apps and Lifeline. Each one leads to a short series of big choices that ends in something getting done.

AGENCY learns what you usually choose, like Friday's pad thai, your pharmacy, or the phrases you say most, and offers it first with a plain reason: “4 of your last 5 Fridays”. You can see, change or erase everything it remembers, and it stays on your Mac.

The prototype's simpler task screen is shown here; the new Home is in progress.

✓Works in the prototype today

Do real tasks, with your approval

Say what you want with a few looks, and an AI agent (Claude) plans the steps and carries them out: ordering food, filling in and signing forms, booking appointments, sending messages.

Before anything that matters (sending, paying, signing, calling, submitting, deleting, sharing your details, changing settings or installing) it stops and shows you exactly what will happen. Your approval covers that exact action; if anything changes, it asks again. Afterwards it checks that the task really worked.

It never types, reads or stores your passwords, two-factor codes or card numbers.

Today with simulated services; the AI agent for your real apps is being built.

◔Being built

Your eyes work in your apps and browser

An eye-control layer floats over every app. Your gaze snaps to real buttons in Mail, Finder, Chrome or any web page, and small targets get a zoom or a “which one?” picker, so an ordinary webcam is precise enough to use a normal Mac.

Help, Stop and Home stay on screen in every app.

Eye control already works on AGENCY's own screens in the prototype.

◔Being built

Talk, in your own voice

Pick words and phrases with your eyes and AGENCY says them out loud, in your own voice if you've set up Apple's Personal Voice.

On phone calls, the other person hears you through text-to-speech while you choose replies with your eyes. AGENCY tells them that a synthetic voice is speaking for you.

✓Works in the prototype today

Lifeline: help, one look away

Close your eyes for about a second, three times, or look at Help. After an 8-second chance to cancel, Lifeline contacts your people one after another, and keeps going, round after round, until someone answers “I'm on my way”.

It also raises the alarm by itself if your screen goes silent or a check-in goes unanswered. The person who comes sees a short card: how you communicate, what to check first, how to get in.

Contacts are simulated phones until someone sets up real ones.

Next: Safety and privacy

Safety and privacy

You stay in control. In plain words:

  • Your camera stays on your Mac

    Camera video is processed on your Mac and thrown away. It's never stored and never sent anywhere.

  • Nothing important happens without you

    Sending, paying, signing, calling, submitting, deleting and sharing your details all wait for your approval of that exact action. Stop works from every screen.

  • Simulated until you choose

    Out of the box, shops, phones and messages are practice versions. Nobody real is contacted and nothing is bought until you, or a helper, deliberately set up the real thing.

  • No passwords in the AI's hands

    AGENCY never types, reads or keeps passwords, two-factor codes or card numbers. It uses the accounts you're already signed in to, with your say-so.

  • Not a medical device

    AGENCY OS isn't a medical device or a ventilator alarm and hasn't been clinically tested. Keep your existing alarms and care routines.

  • Not an emergency service

    Lifeline calls the people you choose until one of them says they're coming. It never calls 911 or other emergency services by itself.

Read the full privacy policy, and how Lifeline is designed and what has and hasn't been tested in LIFELINE.md.

Next: Who it's for

Who it's for

People who can move their eyes, and the people around them.

AGENCY OS is for people living with advanced ALS, locked-in syndrome, a high spinal cord injury, severe cerebral palsy, or anything else that takes away hands and voice but leaves the eyes.

Not being able to communicate is dangerous in care: in a review of 2,355 hospital charts, patients with communication problems were three times as likely to have a preventable adverse event (Bartlett et al., CMAJ 2008). Every part of AGENCY is judged by one question: is this safe and usable for someone who can't move or speak, and can't quickly undo a mistake?

For caregivers and family

  • You can set everything up with a mouse and keyboard; the person can carry on by eye.
  • If you're a Lifeline contact, you don't need an app or an account. You get a message with a personal link to a plain page: I'm on my way, or I can't come.
  • Approvals, memory and the history of every task are there for you both to see.
  • The setup guide walks through installing AGENCY and giving it the permissions it needs.

Next: Download

Download

Get AGENCY OS for your Mac

Checking for the latest version…

Every version of AGENCY OS is on its releases page on GitHub.

Open the releases page on GitHub

What you need

  • macOS 13 Ventura or later
  • A Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) or an Intel processor
  • A webcam: the one built into a MacBook or iMac works
  • Google Chrome, for eye control on web pages (other apps work without it)
  • An Anthropic API key for tasks the AI agent plans itself. Without one, AGENCY runs its built-in tasks only.
Which Mac do I have?
  1. Click the Apple menu in the top-left corner of the screen, then About This Mac.
  2. If it lists a Chip such as Apple M1, M2, M3 or M4, you haveApple silicon.
  3. If it lists a Processor with “Intel” in its name, you have Intel.
  4. The same window shows your macOS version: it needs to be 13 (Ventura) or later.
If macOS says it can't open AGENCY

Until AGENCY OS is signed with an Apple Developer ID, macOS blocks it the first time. You only need to do this once per version.

  1. Open the downloaded .dmg and drag AGENCY into Applications.
  2. Open AGENCY from Applications. macOS says it can't verify it. Click Done (notMove to Bin).
  3. Open System Settings, then Privacy & Security. Scroll down toSecurity. Next to “AGENCY was blocked to protect your Mac”, clickOpen Anyway, and enter your Mac password or use Touch ID.
  4. Open AGENCY again and click Open Anyway once more.

On macOS 13 or 14 you can instead Control-click AGENCY in Applications, choose Open, thenOpen.

After each update of an unsigned build, macOS forgets that it allowed AGENCY to use Accessibility and Screen Recording. Turn them back on as in the setup guide. Signed builds don't have this problem.

To check the file is exactly the one we published, open Terminal and runshasum -a 256 ~/Downloads/ followed by the file's name. The result must match the SHA-256 shown above.

Questions

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a special eye tracker?

No. AGENCY is built around an ordinary webcam, like the one in a MacBook. Webcam eye tracking is approximate, so AGENCY uses big, well-spaced choices, snaps your gaze to the nearest button, and offers zoom for small ones. It measures how well calibration went and tells you honestly. Dedicated eye trackers aren't supported yet.

What if eye tracking doesn't work well for me?

AGENCY also works with a single switch (one button or a long blink, with choices highlighted in turn), with a head pointer, and with a mouse or keyboard for a helper. Every screen works with every one of these.

Will it do things without asking me?

Not anything that matters. Sending, paying, signing, calling, submitting, deleting, sharing your details, changing settings and installing all need your approval of the exact action. The approve button appears away from where you were looking, after a short pause, so a lingering look can't approve by accident. Stop halts everything at once, from any screen.

Does Lifeline call 911?

No. AGENCY never contacts emergency services by itself. Lifeline contacts the people you choose, and keeps contacting them until one of them says they're coming. They can call for an ambulance. Lifeline is not an emergency service and not a medical alarm, and it doesn't replace your ventilator's alarms.

Is my camera video uploaded anywhere?

No. Camera frames are processed on your Mac and thrown away. They are never stored and never sent anywhere, including to the AI.

What does the AI see?

Only what a task you started needs. While it works, AGENCY may send the AI the text of your request and screenshots of the app it's working in. Screenshots aren't kept by default. Text on web pages, emails and documents is treated as information, never as instructions: if a page tries to give the agent orders, it stops and shows you.

AI tasks need an Anthropic API key, and Anthropic's terms apply to what's sent. Without a key, AGENCY runs its built-in tasks only.

Does it cost anything?

Downloading AGENCY OS from this page costs nothing, and there's nothing to buy here. If you use AI tasks, Anthropic bills the account whose API key you use.

Is it a medical device?

No. AGENCY OS is not a medical device, a ventilator alarm or an emergency service, and it hasn't been clinically tested. It hasn't yet been evaluated with the people it's built for; that study is the next big piece of work.

Does it work on Windows, iPad or Linux?

Not yet. It relies on macOS accessibility features to control every app. Tell us what you'd use, and we'll write back if that changes.
